title: Graceful Shedder: Operational Playbook for Burst Fairness & Limiter Outage Recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We’ve observed two correlated failure modes in regional limiter components during sustained tenant bursts: 1) transient limiter outages (control-plane flaps) that cause widespread request spikes after recovery, and 2) imbalanced shedding that starves low-latency interactive traffic in favor of high-throughput batch jobs. This ticket creates an operational playbook and control primitives to: define SLO-aligned shedding behavior, coordinate multi-region circuit-breaker transitions, and ensure graceful recovery when quota services are degraded or temporarily unavailable. Goals: (a) define deterministic SLO thresholds and decision points for circuit breakers and soft-shed policies; (b) implement a coordinated recovery protocol so KV leases, token pools, and cached admissions do not create synchronized bursts on failback; (c) add telemetry and dashboards to detect pre-failure divergence in fairness metrics; (d) document a runbook with rollback/mitigation actions and chaos-testing scenarios. The output is a single canonical playbook used by on-call, SRE, and platform engineers plus a set of small infra changes (feature flags and telemetry hooks) to be rolled with runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: SLO trigger definitions documented: latency and error-rate thresholds per tenant tier and region
Circuit-breaker states and transitions defined with explicit hysteresis windows (open, probing, closed) and cross-region propagation rules
Soft-shed policy implemented: reserve fraction for interactive traffic, proportional fairness heuristic for remaining capacity
Recovery protocol implemented: staggered token rehydration, randomized lease reintroduction, and backpressure ramp-up to avoid synchronized bursts
End-to-end telemetry: fairness_score, reserved_utilization, limiter_health, rehydrate_events emitted and visible on dashboards
Playbook validated by automated chaos test suite (multi-region limiter outage simulation) with a post-mortem template populated by the test run

2026-03-02 | Aisha Patel: Design decision log — circuit-breaker propagation will be eventual (gossip-broadcast) with a 30s anti-flap window. Rationale: strict synchronous propagation increases coupling and risk of global fail-open during region reconcilation.

2026-03-05 | Daniel Kim: Prototype of staggered rehydrate implemented. Strategy: on limiter recovery, rehydrate token leases via randomized backoff per-tenant with exponential ramp (base 100ms, cap 5s). Added FF runtime.feature.graceful_rehydrate. Metrics emitted on first gated deploy in staging.

2026-03-10 | On-call (Maeve O'Connor): Observed test run where naive rehydrate caused a 12% traffic surge to origin services. With the staged rehydrate, peak was reduced to 2.4% and latency SLO preserved. Attaching logs to PR.
